audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven rows disagree with the chart the already-audited mirror committed to.
audit.why: The irelia__tryndamere audit's note is explicit: this side must land Tryndamere / Skill / Skill / Tryndamere / Irelia / Skill / Tryndamere — Tryndamere 3, Skill 3, Irelia 1, with Irelia owning level 6 and Tryndamere owning level 1, levels 4-5 and 2+ items. Level 6 is hers because Vanguard's Edge walls off a champion with no dash and Marks him for a free Bladesurge.
audit.corrected: Tryndamere, Skill, Skill, Tryndamere, Irelia, Skill, Tryndamere — six matched full/content pairs plus ratings, as one atomic group.

audit.why: Bladesurge 10/9/8/7/6s at 15 mana, Defiant Dance 20/18/16/14/12s, Flawless Duet 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s, Vanguard's Edge 125/105/85s. Defiant Dance's 20s at rank 1 against Spinning Slash's 12s is the concrete gap the lane is fought in.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into spikes, whys[3], mid and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Defiant Dance is called a 'parry' that 'blocks your key auto' in spikes[0], spikes[2], mid and wants.foe[1]. It blocks nothing.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Irelia charges a strike that deals more damage as she charges. She takes reduced physical damage during the charge.' It is a damage-reduction window, not a block — and it reduces physical damage specifically, which is the entire Tryndamere kit. A player waiting for a 'parry animation' to end is watching for something that does not exist; the right cue is the charge itself.
audit.corrected: Defiant Dance reduces physical damage while she charges it — your crits are exactly what it is for.

audit.whatIsWrong: Vanguard's Edge's wall was never mentioned, and the page has no Flash advice.
audit.why: 'Afterwards the blades form a wall that will damage and slow enemies that walk through it.' Tryndamere has no dash — Spinning Slash needs a target unit — so the wall, not the burst, is what actually kills him. Its Mark also refreshes Bladesurge straight back onto him.
audit.corrected: Hold Flash for the wall, not the damage; the Mark refreshes her Bladesurge.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ionian Fervor and Bladesurge's healing were both absent.
audit.why: The passive stacks attack speed whenever her spells hit and adds on-hit damage at max stacks, so every short trade you allow makes the next one worse. Bladesurge heals her on each dash, which is what Grievous Wounds is actually fighting here — armour is already half-answered by Defiant Dance.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds turns her tempo off, not armour.

edits.after: Level 3 is even — her Q resets answer your spin, and neither can disengage.

edits.before: At level 4 her stacked passive and W parry keep the edge with her.

edits.before: Irelia's level 3-4 is her power window — once she has Q Bladesurge resets off minions and W Defiant Dance parry, she can dash through the wave onto you and block your key auto. Don't fight into a full wave, and hold E Spinning Slash to disengage rather than to commit.
edits.after: Defiant Dance does not block anything — she takes reduced physical damage while she charges it, which is aimed squarely at your crits. It is 20s at rank 1 — step out of the charge and re-enter the moment it ends, then all-in with Bladesurge also spent.

edits.before: Even here, but you tilt it — R Undying Rage lets you survive her E Flawless Duet stun combo and R Vanguard's Edge burst, then Q-heal back. If she blows her combo and you ult through it, you win the reset.
edits.after: Vanguard's Edge is 125s at rank 1 and leaves a wall behind you that damages and slows — you have no dash, so hold Flash for the wall, not the damage. Its Mark also refreshes Bladesurge straight back onto you.

edits.before: Your crit spike catches up to her tempo — she stacks passive off short trades, so avoid feeding her resets and instead all-in when her Q dash charges and W parry are down, where your sustained autos out-damage her.
edits.after: Ionian Fervor stacks attack speed every time a spell of hers lands, and at max stacks adds damage on hit — so every short trade you allow makes the next one worse. All-in on Defiant Dance's 20s, not between her casts.

edits.before: Levels 3-4 are Irelia's spike: with Q resets and W parry she dashes through minions onto you and blocks your autos, so don't fight into a full wave — level 5-6 evens out as R Undying Rage lets you survive her stun combo.
edits.after: Level 3 is a coin flip: Bladesurge refreshes off any Marked target or kill, so a full wave is a free path onto you. Defiant Dance cuts physical damage while charging rather than blocking a hit — wait it out instead of trading into it.

edits.before: From first item onward you take over — your crit sustain out-damages her short-trade tempo, R negates her E-R burst, and continuous autos plus Q healing win the extended fight as long as you deny her minion resets.
edits.after: Bladesurge heals her on every dash, so Grievous Wounds is what turns her tempo off, not armour — her Defiant Dance already answers armour. Fight in open space with no minions to reset on and the extended fight is yours.
